identityLeakageWarning: Names, places and exact dates are removed where practical. Pretraining may still reveal identity; identity guessing is not rewarded.

cases.cutoff: after two full-size gliders substantially underperform respected aerodynamic calculations, before new wind-tunnel data are collected

packet.pressure: A small team is trying to build a controlled heavier-than-air flying machine. Their control concept works in tests, but two full-size gliders generate far less lift than predicted from respected published aerodynamic tables. A prominent rival institution has achieved powered flight with small unmanned models and is scaling toward a full-size machine.
availableEvidence: The team's 1900 and 1901 gliders are structurally sound and controllable but lift is much lower than calculated.
Increasing wing size/curvature did not solve the lift mismatch and introduced control problems.
Published coefficients were measured on different wing shapes/conditions and have been treated as authoritative.
The rival's small powered models have flown successfully, but structural/control requirements will change with full scale and a human pilot.
The team can still conduct glider tests, small model tests and construct simple measurement apparatus.
liveRoutes: accept published coefficients and add more engine power
build a wind tunnel/balance system and remeasure lift/drag across many wing shapes before another full-scale design
use one more full-size glider as an intermediate generalization test before adding power
copy the successful rival model geometry and scale it directly
focus only on inherent stability and abandon active control
abandon powered-flight research as the data conflict is too severe
constraints: the team has modest workshop capability but can build custom experimental apparatus

cases.hiddenOutcome: The team builds wind-tunnel balances, tests many wing shapes, corrects aerodynamic coefficients and then validates the new data in a 1902 full-size glider with improved three-axis control before adding power. The rival's quarter-scale powered model succeeds but its full-size machine crashes twice in 1903. Controlled powered flight is achieved only after measurement, scale and control are jointly closed.

cases.cutoff: after a very sensitive interferometer again fails to find the expected directional ether-wind signal, before later contraction/relativity frameworks

packet.pressure: Electromagnetic wave theory works extremely well and is commonly interpreted as propagation through a reference medium. Earth's known orbital motion should then create a small directional light-travel difference. A new high-sensitivity optical interferometer, carefully isolated and rotated, repeatedly finds essentially none of the predicted signal.
availableEvidence: The apparatus sensitivity is substantially above that of an earlier null experiment and uses a long effective optical path.
The expected shift follows from a specific ether-motion representation plus known Earth motion.
The null persists while the interferometer itself can resolve much smaller optical/length effects in other uses.
Electromagnetic equations remain empirically powerful; discarding the reference medium may require rethinking moving-frame kinematics, not merely one optical parameter.
Material deformation, incomplete ether entrainment or other compensating effects are logically possible but currently unconstrained.
liveRoutes: declare the null an apparatus failure and stop using it
repeat/rotate/seasonally vary the interferometer to bound residual ether drift more tightly
retain ether and derive a concrete material/contraction mechanism with new predictions
treat the null as a constraint on kinematics and search for a representation with no detectable privileged frame while preserving successful electrodynamics
add arbitrary compensating parameters until the expected shift disappears
ignore the null because the theory is too successful elsewhere
constraints: no direct access to an ether medium exists
precision optical experiments are available but modern atomic clocks/lasers are not
theory must preserve the successful electrodynamic phenomena already explained
one null experiment cannot by itself validate every feature of a replacement theory

cases.hiddenOutcome: The null remains. FitzGerald/Lorentz-style contraction/electron frameworks retain ether while explaining the null; Lorentz transformations become increasingly powerful. In 1905 a new kinematic representation removes a privileged ether frame and reconstructs simultaneity/space/time while preserving electrodynamics. The original experimenters do not immediately interpret their own null this way, and the interferometer remains valuable for unrelated precision measurements.

cases.cutoff: after a laboratory high-pressure catalytic ammonia process is demonstrated and acquired by a chemical company, before industrial plant closure

packet.pressure: A laboratory process can synthesize ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen under high pressure, temperature and a catalyst. The company wants continuous industrial production at orders-of-magnitude larger throughput, but the lab apparatus/catalyst/feed assumptions may not survive scale.
availableEvidence: Laboratory equilibrium/rate behavior is reproducible at elevated pressure and temperature.
The laboratory catalyst works but relies on expensive/scarce materials.
Industrial-scale pressure vessels, compressors, valves and seals must run continuously under hot hydrogen-rich gas.
Real feed gases contain impurities that may poison catalysts.
Alternative nitrogen-fixation routes already exist and provide a strong industrial baseline, though they have high energy/material costs.
liveRoutes: geometrically enlarge the laboratory apparatus directly
build staged pilot units while separately testing pressure-vessel materials under hot hydrogen
run a broad catalyst search for cheaper abundant materials under realistic feed impurities
develop gas-purification and continuous heat/recycle loops as explicit subsystems
abandon high pressure and scale the existing alternative nitrogen-fixation route
treat scale-up as implementation and optimize only construction cost
constraints: continuous operation exposes failure modes absent from short lab experiments
full plant trials are extremely expensive

cases.hiddenOutcome: Industrial scale-up becomes a distinct research program: new pressure-vessel/material construction is required, expensive laboratory catalysts are replaced by scalable iron-based catalysts after broad search, feed-gas purification and continuous process engineering become essential, and stepwise larger units lead to a 1913 industrial ammonia plant.

cases.cutoff: after a standardized automobile is already built by stationary skilled teams and a small moving magneto-assembly experiment greatly improves throughput, before full chassis flow is adopted

packet.pressure: Demand for a standardized automobile is exceeding output. Current stationary assembly uses small skilled teams that can perform many tasks on each vehicle. A recent experiment on one subassembly divided work into a few repeated tasks and moved the unit between stations, sharply reducing labor time.
availableEvidence: The existing stationary system produces working vehicles and is flexible when local fitting/rework is needed.
The product design is unusually standardized and demand volume is high.
Many parts are already manufactured to tight enough tolerances for limited interchangeability, but a mismatch at one station can halt downstream flow.
The moving subassembly trial greatly improved throughput despite narrower worker tasks.
Other industries use sequential flow/conveyance, but a whole automobile chassis is larger and has uneven task times.
Narrow repetitive work may raise dissatisfaction/turnover even if vehicle throughput rises.
liveRoutes: retain flexible stationary teams and simply add more parallel bays
expand moving flow one subsystem at a time while measuring cycle time/bottlenecks/quality
move the full chassis immediately through fixed specialized stations
build hybrid cells where variable/fitting work remains flexible and repetitive stable tasks flow
increase product variety to keep workers flexible
reject specialization because a general worker/production system is more reusable
constraints: part interchangeability is necessary but imperfect
worker experience/turnover and production cost are distinct objectives

cases.hiddenOutcome: Flow is expanded from subassemblies to chassis during 1913. Combined with interchangeability, specialized machinery and process balancing, moving assembly reduces Model T build time dramatically. The result is highly scoped to standardized high-volume production and coexists with repetitive work and serious labor-turnover pressure; later high-variety production requires different organization.
